speaker: judith_sadler
text: Sit, Will. You stand in my bakehouse like a man waiting to be paid for it. The shoulder has been in the bread oven since the second batch.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I am in good time, and I have brought three critics who were promised a pie on Thursday.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: I was promised the corner with the most crust. Hamnet says the corner is his because he thought of it first.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I thought of it on Thursday, which is older than thinking of it in the lane.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Thursday is not a claim on a pie. Sit down, both of you, before Mistress Sadler cuts it to spite you.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Let her cut it as she likes. They have argued the corner all the way up the lane.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: Anne. He slept, didn't he.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The second lesson, with his eyes open. I let him.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Sit, godson. The mutton will not come to you.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: There. And this, before any of you begins on London prices.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: You'll have heard in London that bakers are thieves. Weigh it. It's what the assize gives for a penny with wheat where it is. The loaf is small because the wheat is dear, and I'm not the villain of it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: In Southwark they blamed the butter-wives, and whipped the boys who said so.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: What is the wheat, then, if a penny buys this?

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Six-and-thirty shillings the quarter, new wheat, at the Cross on Thursday. When it stands there, the bailiff weighs my penny loaf like gold dust, and the poor curse me for an ounce short.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: And what do they blame you for, in London?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The Lord Mayor blames us for the boys.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: The boys. Lord, Will.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: I had not finished considering it.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: You may consider it over the cheese. The pie is going while it is hot. Corner to the one who can hold her tongue for a minute, and that will not be either twin.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Then Susanna gets it, and she did not even race us for it.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: She can have the corner. I want to know about Tuesday.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Tuesday is the frame. Seven of the clock, twelve men, poles and two ropes, and the carpenter to call the lift. Ale after, at my cousin's charge. Your twenty shillings is already in the oak.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I'll be there at seven.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: He will be there. Whether he is of any use to a post is a different question. Give me the loaf.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Weigh it, Anne. I'll abide the scale. I will not abide being the cause of a thin year.

speaker: judith_sadler
text: Eat, the pack of you. The cheese is the last of what kept, and I am not baking another pie because a child has invented a corner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The pie is worth the argument. Tell your cousin I bring my brother's back as well as mine. Richard lifts as a man who lifts every day.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Bring him. Twelve is twelve, and a glover's shoulders are as good as a player's, and a deal more honest about it.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: If we go now, is there pie left at home?

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: There is pie if we are quicker than the talking. The talking has had the cheese.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Come. They are looking at their hands, and that means we are to go ahead.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Go on. Argue it in the lane, and leave us the cheese.
